we provide a theoretical foundation to guide the choice of weak supervision methods in disentanglement learning, and we show that weak supervision can indeed guarantee disentangement under some circumstances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disentanglements conferred by weak supervision are not always guaranteed, even when weak supervision is paired with a learning algorithm with known disentanglement guarantee.
weak supervision is not a panacea, but can be an important tool when coupled with a learning algorithm that is amenable to disentanglement, and when used with the right type of supervision.
